page: Amazon Web Services r8g.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by an ARM64 AWS Neoverse-V2 processor. The instance features 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with a dedicated CPU allocation running at 2.8 GHz. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights strong memory subsystem performance, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Large-block read-only memory bandwidth is strong at 189.8 GB/sec, and single-core performance is strong in Geekbench and text processing. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is also strong. Conversely, the instance exhibits weak performance in PassMark CPU encryption and text generation for small language models, alongside poor prompt processing speeds for medium-sized models. Other benchmarks, including multi-core CPU performance and database operations, fall within the average range.

The r8g.2xlarge leverages the ARM64 architecture to deliver high memory density per core without hyperthreading. This configuration is suitable for memory-intensive workloads such as caching layers, in-memory databases, and text processing applications that benefit from high memory bandwidth. However, it is less suited for cryptographic-heavy operations or large-scale language model inference due to specific benchmark limitations in those areas.
